channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.desc: Chef Joseph Lidgerwood?s class is? A Little Too Special! A K-FOOD experience crafted like no other ? Now Open! As global interest in Korean culture continues to thrive, K-FOOD has become one of its most compelling pillars. And today, people aren?t just curious about how it tastes. They want to learn how it?s made. Joseph Lidgerwood, chef-owner of the Michelin two-star restaurant EVETT, is an Australian chef who has developed a deep connection to Korea?s traditional jang and its ingredients. Now, he?s ready to share what he calls the ?the true taste of Korea.? Each episode welcomes a new group of participants from around the world, learning the all-time favorites such as Korean fried chicken, jaeyuk bokkeum, ganjang gejang, godeungeo kimchijjim, and bajirak sujebi, all reimagined through Joseph?s unique style. The atmosphere in the kitchen, shaped by curiosity, focus, and genuine interaction between Joseph and his students, often becomes as memorable as the food they create. You?ll take home the recipes, of course. But what truly sets this class apart is the moments shared along the way, the laughter, the discoveries, and the way flavor bridges cultures. Experience the depth, joy, and creativity of K-FOOD in Joseph?s A Little Too Special: K-FOOD Class!

Discover Korean travel expressions in an engaging and entertaining way with skits performed by ONF?s Hyo-jin, Seung-jun, Wyatt, and Alexa. With clear and accessible explanations from Hye-rim of the Wonder Girls, a graduate of Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, you?ll systematically improve your Korean!

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: K-FOOD CLASS
channel.desc: Chef Joseph Lidgerwood?s class is? A Little Too Special! A K-FOOD experience crafted like no other ? Now Open! As global interest in Korean culture continues to thrive, K-FOOD has become one of its most compelling pillars. And today, people aren?t just curious about how it tastes. They want to learn how it?s made. Joseph Lidgerwood, chef-owner of the Michelin two-star restaurant EVETT, is an Australian chef who has developed a deep connection to Korea?s traditional jang and its ingredients. Now, he?s ready to share what he calls the ?the true taste of Korea.? Each episode welcomes a new group of participants from around the world, learning the all-time favorites such as Korean fried chicken, jaeyuk bokkeum, ganjang gejang, godeungeo kimchijjim, and bajirak sujebi, all reimagined through Joseph?s unique style. The atmosphere in the kitchen, shaped by curiosity, focus, and genuine interaction between Joseph and his students, often becomes as memorable as the food they create. You?ll take home the recipes, of course. But what truly sets this class apart is the moments shared along the way, the laughter, the discoveries, and the way flavor bridges cultures. Experience the depth, joy, and creativity of K-FOOD in Joseph?s A Little Too Special: K-FOOD Class!

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE B
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Verdi ? La Traviata
channel.desc: Nach anf?nglicher Ablehnung seitens des Publikums wurde Verdis einzigartige La Traviata mit der Zeit doch eins seiner meist gefeierten Werke. Zentrales Thema der ist die tragische Liebesgeschichte um Violetta Val?ry und Alfredo. Die reiche Kurtisane hat scheinbar alles, was das Herz begehrt: Geld, Freunde und Liebhaber, doch als sie sich in den jungen Alfredo verliebt, zieht sie damit ?rger auf sich. Giorgio Germont, Alfredos Vater, will die Beziehung der beiden nicht zulassen und verlangt von Violetta, seinen Sohn f?r immer zu verlassen? La Traviata ist eine , die Verdi dank einzigartiger Musik und Darstellung von Menschlichkeit und tiefgr?ndiger Charaktere zu einer Legende machte. Regisseur David McVicar versetzte das Drama in eine Welt voller romantischer Elemente, die dennoch eine moderne Perspektive annimmt. Gemeinsam mit dem Orchester und Chor des Teatro Real und gefeierten Solisten wie Ermonela Jaho und Francesco Demuro meistert Dirigent Renato Palumbo die bekannte italienische .

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Beethoven ? Sinfonie Nr. 6 in F-Dur: op. 68
channel.desc: Der Schweizer Dirigent Philippe Jordan und das Orchestre de l'Op?ra national de Paris nahmen den kompletten Zyklus der Sinfonien von Ludwig van Beethoven in den Jahren 2014-2015 auf. In dieser Auff?hrung dirigiert Jordan Beethovens Sinfonie Nr. 6 in F-Dur, Op. 68, auch bekannt als die Pastorale Sinfonie. Der Komponist schrieb das Werk unmittelbar nach der Vollendung seiner Sinfonie Nr. 5. Beide Werke wurden im Dezember 1808 im selben uraufgef?hrt. Die Sinfonie Nr. 6 besteht aus f?nf S?tzen, wobei die letzten drei S?tze ohne Pause gespielt werden. Jeder Satz tr?gt einen Titel, der eine Szene aus dem Landleben suggeriert. Die fr?hliche Atmosph?re der ersten drei S?tze wird durch einen gewaltigen vierten Satz unterbrochen: Sturm, besonders dargestellt durch die Piccolofl?ten, Blechbl?ser und Pauken. Der Sturm l?sst am Ende des Satzes nach, woraufhin die Ruhe im letzten Satz zur?ckkehrt. Diese Auff?hrung wurde 2015 in der Op?ra Bastille in Paris, Frankreich, aufgezeichnet.

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Mozart ? Violinkonzert Nr. 4
channel.desc: Les Dissonances ist ein K?nstlerkollektiv, das 2004 vom Geiger David Grimal gegr?ndet wurde. Das Ensemble ohne Dirigenten besteht aus Musikern der renommiertesten europ?ischen Orchester, internationalen Solisten und jungen Talenten. In dieser Auff?hrung spielt Les Dissonances Wolfgang Amadeus Mozarts Violinkonzert Nr. 4 in D-Dur, K. 218. Grimal, der Geiger, tritt als Solist auf. Mit Ausnahme des ersten Violinkonzerts komponierte Mozart seine anderen vier Violinkonzerte 1775, als er meister am Salzburger Hof war. Unter seinen f?nf en ist das Violinkonzert Nr. 4 eines der bekanntesten. Diese Auff?hrung wurde 2014 in der Cit? de la Musique in Frankreich aufgezeichnet. Mit dabei: Les Dissonances.

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Brahms ? Tragischen Ouvert?re in d-Moll: Op. 81
channel.desc: Der Maggio Musicale Fiorentino (Florentiner Musikmai) ist das ?lteste Opern- und Musikfestival Italiens. Es wurde 1933 gegr?ndet, urspr?nglich mit dem Ziel, zeitgen?ssische und vergessene Opern zu pr?sentieren. Im Laufe der Jahre hat sich das Spektrum jedoch erheblich erweitert, und Orchesterkonzerte sind l?ngst ein fester Bestandteil des Festivals. Im Rahmen der Ausgabe 2021, dirigiert Maestro Daniel Harding das Orchestra del Maggio Musicale Fiorentino bei einer Auff?hrung der Tragischen Ouvert?re in d-Moll, Op. 81 von Johannes Brahms. Brahms komponierte seine ouvert?re im Sommer 1880. Mit ihrem d?steren und st?rmischen Charakter k?nnte sie als ernstes Gegenst?ck zu seiner freudigeren Akademischen Festouvert?re, Op. 80, betrachtet werden. Diese Auff?hrung wurde 2021 im Teatro del Maggio Musicale Fiorentino in Florenz, Italien, aufgezeichnet.

channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: Antoni Wit dirigiert die Warschauer Philharmoniker in einer performance von Fr?d?ric Chopins Klavierkonzert Nr. 1, Op. 11, und Nr. 2, Op. 21. Die Solisten sind die Pianisten Nikolai Demidenko und Evgeny Kissin. Nach dem ersten gibt Demidenko eine Zugabe und interpretiert Chopins Mazurka Op. 17/4. Kissin vollendet das schlie?lich mit Chopins Et?de Op. 10/12 und dem Walzer in e-Moll, Op. post. Dieses war Teil der Feierlichkeiten anl?sslich des 200. Geburtstag von Chopin im Jahr 2010. Chopin komponierte sein Klavierkonzert Nr. 2 tats?chlich ein Jahr vor dem Klavierkonzert Nr. 1 und vollendete beide Werke im Alter von 20 Jahren, bevor er sein Heimatland Polen in Richtung Paris verlie?. channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: In diesem exquisiten aus der Moskauer Tchaikovsky Concert Hall wird das Russian National Orchestra von Dirigent Michail Pletnjow durch ein Programm mit wunderbaren Suiten von Nikolai Rimski-Korsakow geleitet. Das ist eine Produktion der Moscow Philharmonic Society, die einst der in Sankt Petersburg geborene Komponist Dimitri Schostakowitsch selbst als eine extrem einflussreiche Instanz "in der Entwicklung des musikalischen Lebens [in Russland]" beschrieb. "Sie ist eine Art universit?ts?hnliche Institution, die von hunderten Musikfans und tausenden Musikern frequentiert wird", so Dimitri Schostakowitsch. Die Moscow Philharmonic Society wurde 1922 vom damaligen Kulturabgeordneten des Landes, Anatoli Lunatscharski, gegr?ndet und ist inzwischen Russlands f?hrende Instanz f?r organisation.

channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: Die Pianistin Rachel Breen (USA, 1996) spielt den Marsch aus Sergei Prokofjews "Marsch und Scherzo" aus "Die Liebe zu den drei Orangen", Op. 33ter; Pr?ludium und Walzer in C (Nr. 4) aus Gy?rgy Kurt?gs "J?t?kok" (Spiele), Band 1; Pr?ludium Nr. 23 in F-Dur aus Alexander Skrjabins "24 Pr?ludien", Op. 11; Intermezzo (Nr. 1) aus Prokofjews "Drei St?cke aus Cinderella", Op. 95; Bagatelle Nr. 3 in Es-Dur aus Ludwig van Beethovens "Bagatellen", Op. 126; Fr?d?ric Chopins "Impromptu Nr. 1 in As-Dur", Op. 29; "Wasserklavier" (Nr. 3) aus Luciano Berios "Sechs Encores"; Chopins "Impromptu Nr. 2 in Fis-Dur", Op. 36; "Skazki Nr. 5 in Fis-Moll" aus Nikolai Medtners "6 Skazki" (M?rchen), Op. 51; Et?de Nr. 4 in h-Moll aus Sergei Rachmaninows "?tudes-tableaux", Op. 39; und Pr?ludium Nr. 4 in e-Moll aus Leonid Desyatnikovs "The Songs of Bukovina" (24 Pr?ludien), in der ersten Runde der Klavierausgabe des Concours musical international de Montr?al 2024 (CMIM). Diese Auff?hrung wurde in der Bourgie Hall des Montreal Museum of Fine Arts aufgenommen. Mit dabei: Rachel Breen.

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Beethoven ? Piano Sonata No. 31, Op. 110
channel.desc: Kann es uns gelingen, uns in Beethovens kreativen Geist hineinzuversetzen, besonders in der letzten Phase seines Lebens, als er mit schwerem H?rverlust zu k?mpfen hatte? Tom Beghins neue Aufnahme von Beethovens Klaviersonaten Opus 109, 110 und 111 ist eine k?nstlerische Untersuchung dessen, inwiefern Beethovens Musik durch sein direktes Umfeld gepr?gt wurde, das er sich gemeinsam mit der Hilfe von Kollegen und Freunden schuf. Der Pianist Tom Beghin interpretiert hier nicht nur Beethovens Trilogie pianistischer Meisterwerke auf einem gro?artigen neuen Replikat Beethovens Broadwood-Klavieres, sondern verwendet dabei auch eine Rekonstruktion der Geh?rmaschine, die auf dem Klavier des Komponisten montiert war, damit er weiterhin Musik komponieren und spielen konnte, trotz des schwindenden Geh?rsinns. "Sie h?ren besser, wenn Sie Ihren Kopf unter diese Maschine halten, nicht wahr?", fragte Andr? Stein einst Beethoven. Zwei Jahrhunderte sp?ter k?nnen auch wir unsere K?pfe unter die Maschine halten und uns fragen: H?ren wir Beethoven anders? Beghin zieht uns in das H?rger?t hinein, wo wir die Essenz von Beethovens wilden und unwiderstehlich poetischen musikalischen Eingebungen f?hlen und h?ren. "Inside the Hearing Machine" l?dt uns auf den multisensorischen Spielplatz eines geh?rlosen Komponisten ein, f?r den die Maschine mehr als ein H?rger?t war und der ?ber viel mehr als nur Klang mit seinem Instrument interagierte. Mit dabei: Tom Beghin.

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Meisterwerke entdecken
channel.desc: Mit der Serie "Meisterwerke Entdecken" pr?sentieren wir audiovisuelle Konzertf?hrer der gro?en Meisterwerke der klassischen Musik. Die Serie enth?lt 20 halbst?ndige Dokumentationen ?ber 20 Meisterwerke der Klassik. Angesehene Experten, ber?hmte Solisten und herausragende Dirigenten versetzen Sie zur?ck in die Zeit und an die Orte ihrer Entstehung. In diesem Dokumentarfilm steht Hector Berlioz' Symphonie fantastique im Mittelpunky. Diese "Fantastische Sinfonie" gilt allgemein als eines der wichtigsten und charakteristischsten Werke der Fr?hromantik. Leonard Bernstein nannte es aufgrund seiner halluzinogenen und traumhaften Art "die erste musikalische Reise ins Psychedelische". Der deutsche Musikwissenschaftler Wulf Konold beschreibt die Idee zur Entstehung dieses faszinierenden St?cks.

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Monteverdi ? Madrigale: Buch III
channel.desc: Der italienische Komponist Claudio Monteverdi (1567-1643) schrieb in einem Zeitraum von f?nf Jahrzehnten neun B?cher mit Madrigalen. Er trug ma?geblich zur Transformation des Genres von den polyphonen, a cappella Madrigalen der Sp?trenaissance zu den "concertato" Madrigalen des fr?hen Barock bei, indem er den Schwerpunkt auf die Ausdruckskraft der Musik legte. Im Jahr 2011 begannen der britische Tenor Paul Agnew und das renommierte Barockmusikensemble Les Arts Florissants, acht B?cher von Monteverdis Madrigalen aufzunehmen. In diesem Programm pr?sentiert Les Arts Florissant unter der Leitung von Agnew die Madrigale aus Buch III. Ver?ffentlicht im Jahr 1592, enth?lt das Buch 20 Madrigale f?r f?nf Stimmen. Diese Auff?hrung wurde 2012 in der Cit? de la musique in Paris, Frankreich, aufgenommen.

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Brahms ? 1. Sinfonie: Op. 68
channel.desc: Franz Welser-M?st leitet das Cleveland Orchestra in einem von Brahms 1. Sinfonie im Rahmen der BBC Proms 2014. Nur wenige klassische Kompositionen haben einen derartig langatmigen Entstehungsprozess vorzuweisen wie Brahms erste Sinfonie. Der Komponist hatte bereits 1855, im Alter von nur 22 Jahren erste Ideen zum Werk, doch bis zu seiner Ver?ffentlichung von 1876 durchlief es zahlreiche Revisionen. Obgleich Brahms von seiner Angst, in Gegenwart von Beethoven in Vergessenheit zu raten gehemmt wurde, lie? er sich von seinem Umfeld schlie?lich zur Ver?ffentlichung bewegen. Unter seinen bekannten Unterst?tzern waren beispielsweise Komponistin Clara Schumann und Musikologe Philipp Spitta. Teil dieser Performance ist auch die britische Premiere von J?rg Widmanns 'Fl?te en suite', interpretiert von Solist Joshua Smith. Aufgenommen in der Royal Albert Hall in London.

channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: Das Bolschoi Theaterballett interpretiert Dmitri Schostakowitschs "Golden Age", ein in zwei Akten, mit einer Choreografie von Juri Grigorowitsch. In den 1920ern erlaubte die Neue ?konomische Politik (NEP) es, aktiv private Gesch?fte und Handel zu betreiben, was dazu f?hrte, dass zwielichtige Gesch?fte und kleinkriminelle Ganoven aufbl?hten wie nie zuvor. Dort unterhalten Rita, eine junge T?nzerin, die sich als Mademoiselle Margot ausgibt, und ihr Partner Jacques, eigentlich Yashka, die gemeinsam eine lokale Banditengruppe anf?hren, ein Publikum aus "Schnellebenden". channel.desc: Dina Ivanova (1994, Russia) performs Franz Liszt's Piano Concerto No. 1 (S124), during the final of the 11th International Franz Liszt Piano Competition, held in TivoliVredenburg, Utrecht 2017. The competition actively presents, develops and promotes piano talents from around the world. In doing so, it has become one of the prominent gateways to the international professional classical music scene for young musicians. The International Franz Liszt Piano Competition was founded in 1986 in the Netherlands and since has built a reputation as one of the world's most prestigious piano competitions.

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Giuseppe Verdi: Nabucco
channel.desc: Der israelische Dirigent Daniel Oren leitet das Orchester der Arena di Verona in einer gro?artigen Interpretation von Giuseppe Verdis Nabucco von 2017. Verdis dritte ? und sein erster echter Erfolg ? wurde 1842 f?r das Teatro alla Scala in Mailand kreiert, dem damaligen Epizentrum des "Risorgimento" und Hauptstadt des italienischen Nationalismus zu einem Zeitpunkt an dem die Verfechter der italienischen Unabh?ngigkeit von der ?sterreichischen Besetzung sich nach und nach Geh?r verschafften. Ein Auszug aus Va, pensiero, sull'ali dorate (deutsch: "Flieg, Gedanke, auf goldenen Schwingen"), den die Juden im dritten Akt singen, nachdem sie durch Nabuchodonosor aus Babylon verbannt wurden und um ihre Heimat trauern, fand schnell Anklang unter den italienischen Nationalisten und gilt seitdem als Symbol der italienischen Nationalidentit?t. Daniel Oren gilt als echter Kenner Verdis und gern gesehener Gast der Arena di Verona. Er dirigiert dieses "lyrisch epische Werk", das den Italienern so sehr am Herzen liegt, mit gro?em Elan. Unter den Solisten sind George Gagnidze, Susanna Branchini, Nino Surguladze, Rubens Pelizzari und Stanislav Trofimov. Diese Aufnahme entstand w?hrend einer Auff?hrung 2017 in der Arena di Verona. Mit dabei: Sebastian Catana Rubens Pelizzari Stanislav Trofimov Susanna Branchini Nino Surguladze Elena Borin Paolo Antognetti Nicol? Ceriani.

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Saint-Sa?ns ? Intro und Rondo Capriccioso, Op. 28
channel.desc: Die Waldb?hne in Berlin, eines der attraktivsten Freiluft-Amphitheater des europ?ischen Kontinentes, bietet den Sommerkonzerten der Berliner Philharmoniker eine wundersch?ne B?hne. Mit ?ber 22.000 Besuchern geh?rt pro Jahr geh?rt die Waldb?hne zu den beliebtesten Klassik-Veranstaltungsorten der Welt. Die ausgezeichneten MusikerInnen der Berliner Philharmoniker interpretieren gemeinsam mit Solistin Janine Jansen unter der Leitung von Dirigent Neeme J?rvi Saint-Sa?ns' Introduction et Rondo capriccioso en la mineur. Dieses Performance war Teil des ber?hmten Berliner Waldb?hnekonzertes von 2006. Mit dabei: Janine Jansen (Violinistin).

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: IVC 2021
channel.desc: Die Sopranistin Heidi Baumgartner (?sterreich, 1998) und die Pianistin Asuka Tagami (Japan, 1991) f?hren Franz Schuberts "Suleika I" auf, Op. 14 Nr. 1, D. 720; "Er ist's" aus Hugo Wolfs "M?rike-Liedern"; Bart Vismans "Vermeers Gold"; "Sua katselen" (Schau dich an) aus Kaija Saariahos "Leino-Laulut" (Leino-Liedern); und "Pantomime" und "Apparition" aus Claude Debussys "Quatre chansons de jeunesse" beim Halbfinale der International Vocal Competition 2021 ? Lied Duo. Diese Auff?hrung wurde im Het-Noordbrabants-Museum im niederl?ndischen 's-Hertogenbosch aufgenommen.[(96057)]

channel.desc: EWTN News Nightly is our daily news and analysis program presenting breaking Catholic News worldwide, top stories, and daily reports from the White House, Capitol Hill, and Rome. Weekdays at 6 & 9 PM EST. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Daily Mass
channel.desc: The Franciscan Missionaries of the Eternal Word celebrate Mass from the Our Lady of Angels Chapel in Irondale, AL. (LIVE DAILY at 8 am Eastern). (60 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: The Holy Land Rosary
channel.desc: Fr. Mitch Pacwa leads the Sorrowful Mysteries of the Rosary from the actual holy sites and shrines where they took place, bringing the Gospels to life and offering a deeper understanding of the Rosary meditations. (18 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: The Litany Of The Most Precious Blood Of Jesus
channel.desc: Join the Franciscan Missionaries of the Eternal Word at the Shrine of the Most Blessed Sacrament in Hanceville, Alabama, as they recite this beautiful prayer in honor of the Precious Blood of Jesus shed for our salvation. (12 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Black And Roman Catholic
channel.desc: Noah and Dolores talk about how the Pope condemned slavery before the slave trade began. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Mother Angelica Live Classics
channel.desc: Mother talks about showing compassion and forgiveness toward everyone, including our enemies. (60 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: new! Women Of Grace
channel.desc: Fr. Cedric Pisegna is back to give more insight and practical tips from his personal experience and what he?s learned ?on the job,? regarding the spiritual life God desires for us. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: new! Ewtn Pro Life Weekly
channel.desc: EWTN Pro-Life Weekly is a half-hour news and commentary program that covers life issues including abortion, assisted suicide, in vitro fertilization, highlighting the mercy of a culture of life, from a Catholic perspective. This program features interviews, analysis, and actionable steps for viewers to defend the dignity of every human person from conception to natural death. Hosted by Abigail Galv?n. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Ewtn Great Britain On Location
channel.desc: James McCullough and Fr. Andrew Pinsent, Research Director at the University of Oxford, discuss how to cultivate a Life of Grace by accepting suffering, getting rid of clutter in our lives, and dedicating ourselves to prayer. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: In Concert Johann Sebastian Bach?s Mass In B Minor
channel.desc: Philippe Herreweghe conducts the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra in Johann Sebastian Bach?s Mass in B Minor. The performance features the Collegium Vocale Gent and renowned soloists. (120 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Catholic Sphere
channel.desc: Ryan Penney, Roxie Beckles, Daniel Godinez, and Christopher Quinn discuss the many divisions between races and ethnicities in the Church today, and what can be done about them. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: A Travel Guide To Heaven
channel.desc: Host Anthony DeStefano discusses how the resurrected bodies will influence our activities, work, and time in Heaven. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: The Divine Mercy Chaplet For Kids
channel.desc: Animated devotional special for children as Saint Faustina teaches Kristin, Eva, Enrique and Joseph how to pray the Chaplet, an explanation of the Divine Mercy Image and the importance of Confession. (30 minutes).[(96057)]

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Document 72 Hours
channel.desc: The Hokkaido village of Shosanbetsu is home to about 1,000 people and a single convenience store. Residents rely on this store as a source of fresh food and basic necessities, especially in midwinter. Among the customers were a woman who uses a sled to carry her shopping home; an octopus fisherman who shops there three times a day; and a hair stylist who knows everybody in Shosanbetsu. For three days as a blizzard buffeted the area, we spoke to the store's customers to get a glimpse at life in this village.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Matsuri: The Heartbeat Of Japan
channel.desc: Gojinjo Taiko is a wild, powerful performance by masked drummers. It originated 400 years ago in the small coastal community of Nafune-machi in Ishikawa Prefecture. The story goes that, faced with an imminent attack by a powerful warlord, villagers used improvised masks to disguise themselves as oni (demons), and scared away the approaching forces. Gojinjo Taiko is performed not only at the summer matsuri (festival) but at local hotels in everyday life, as a form of community revitalization.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Matsuri: The Heartbeat Of Japan
channel.desc: Gojinjo Taiko is a wild, powerful performance by masked drummers. It originated 400 years ago in the small coastal community of Nafune-machi in Ishikawa Prefecture. The story goes that, faced with an imminent attack by a powerful warlord, villagers used improvised masks to disguise themselves as oni (demons), and scared away the approaching forces. Gojinjo Taiko is performed not only at the summer matsuri (festival) but at local hotels in everyday life, as a form of community revitalization.

channel.desc: Sweet potatoes are a popular food throughout Japan. They're baked, simmered, added to soup, and turned into confectionery. Baked sweet potatoes are a beloved street food. channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Impacts: Climates Change The World
channel.desc: Rising temperatures due to climate change have affected the behavior of bees, with fewer bees and shorter pollination periods, posing a threat to agriculture that could lead to a food crisis.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Design Museum Japan
channel.desc: Hokkaido Prefecture / Takeya Takayuki (Model maker)\nFishing boats in the herring industry?which thrived here until the 1950s?featured swirling decorations that made a big impression on Takeya, a Hokkaido native.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Where We Call Home
channel.desc: We meet two Americans who preserve Japanese traditions. Chris Hinds ensures the safe conduct of Nozawa Onsen's fire festival in Nagano Prefecture, and Andrew Mancabelli crafts Japanese armor in Warabi, Saitama Prefecture.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Time Lapse Japan
channel.desc: The Murakami Kaizoku were seafarers and fighters in the Seto Inland Sea. We explore their history and legacy, with footage from time-lapse creator Shimizu Daisuke. This time, the Kurushima Straits.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Bosai: Science That Can Save Your Life
channel.desc: Japan has a long history of natural disasters. BOSAI explores how to overcome them and save lives with the power of science.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Activate Your Japanese!
channel.desc: Drama \"Xuan Tackles Japan!\"\nTime has passed, and the hotel's autumn campaign has been a success. Rei then tells Xuan that he is quitting his job at the hotel to go to France. Unable to process this sudden revelation, Xuan shrinks from talking to Rei even on the day of his departure. But she knows she needs to talk to him before he leaves, and she hurries after him to the airport. Xuan wants to express her feelings and gratitude to Rei. Will she be able to say what she wants to say? What should she do if she feels unsure of her Japanese?\n\"Onomatopoeia\" -Share Feelings- Kotsukotsu.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Culture Crossroads
channel.desc: Culture Crossroads comprises several regular programs with the theme of creating a multicultural society. They look at international exchange programs and give tips on disaster preparedness.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Hello! Nhk World Japan
channel.desc: In a special feature on Hokkaido, programs looked at the ecology of brown bears, a special bento lunch, and a bountiful landscape formed by rugged natural conditions and pioneering development.

channel.desc: Located in Hokkaido Prefecture in northern Japan is Noboribetsu, a prominent resort of hot springs, or \"onsen\" in Japanese. channel.desc: Drama \"Xuan Tackles Japan!\"\nTime has passed, and the hotel's autumn campaign has been a success. Rei then tells Xuan that he is quitting his job at the hotel to go to France.
